facts.fact: The national Open Data steering committee (COPIL), meeting at the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD), debated a 2026 action plan of the government's Open Data programme that includes enriching and maintaining the national open data portal www.data.gov.ma; the document names no open data policy, strategy or law behind the portal and gives no dataset or publisher count.

facts.fact: The Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) is the organisation publishing a dataset of 1,028 Moroccan startups on data.gov.ma, whose resource was created and last modified on 2025-01-03 (dataset first created 2021-11-16); the document does not say who runs the portal or tie it to an open data policy.

The document shows data.gov.ma operating as a CKAN-based open data portal hosting datasets under an ODbL licence, with ADD as a listed publishing organisation; it does not state who runs the portal or tie it to an open data policy, and gives its date as the 2025-01-03 release.

The portal's own documentation page says the Agence de Developpement du Digital (ADD) manages Morocco's national open data portal and monitors the national Open Data action plan, which the Open Data steering committee (set up December 2019) oversees; no published date, so the page's retrieval date of 2026-08-08 is used.

systems.tiers: national; ministries and public bodies publish through designated Open Data Officers and Data Managers

note: The page describes the 2020 ADD/World Bank readiness-assessment action plan and steering committee but does not say any policy, decree or law was adopted, and names no ministry releasing data nor a dataset count, so no standing fact and no published fact.

facts.fact: The ADD's December 2024 operational manual on open data standards says the national open data portal was launched in 2011, that the Agence de Développement du Digital coordinates the Open Data programme and is responsible for the portal, and that every dataset published there must meet its minimum quality criteria; it states that the portal hosts datasets of some administrations and references datasets on sector portals, names no ministry or agency that has released data and gives no dataset or publisher count, and ties the portal to no open data policy, strategy or law.

facts.fact: The Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) launched the new version of the national open data portal on 2021-12-13, in Arabic and French, as part of implementing the Open Data action plan and Morocco's open government commitments.
On the relaunch the ADD reports about 43% more datasets published and 31% more bodies producing open data, giving no absolute counts; the portal gives access to data from several public bodies.

facts.fact: Morocco's digital transition minister Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni said on 18 February 2025 that a draft decree setting the rules for organising, publishing and governing open public data has been prepared, covering all institutions named in law 31-13.

note: Document states nothing this study asks for this country.
The notice refers to an open data action plan but states no adopted or drafted open data policy, decree or law.

facts.fact: The OGP IRM results report says a legal framework for promoting public open data was still being drafted as a decree by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform and the Digital Development Agency, at the end of the 2021-2023 plan.

The IRM report says the Digital Development Agency, lead for the open data commitment, redesigned and runs the national open data portal data.gov.ma, launched in 2011 and redesigned from December 2021.
The IRM report says by end 2023 the portal held over 500 datasets and 37 institutions were updating datasets on it, according to the Digital Development Agency.
